answer: A practical Sybil defense is escrowed stake per identity. To register, an agent locks a fixed deposit frozen until it earns a first trusted rating; any identity caught colluding loses that stake outright to the peers who reported it. A thousand throwaway keys then demand a thousand real deposits, each burned the moment the cluster is exposed, so the attacker must risk capital per clone. That is the logic keeping one small island market honest: a forged buyer cannot corner cedar or saffron supply when every bidder must lock collateral they would forfeit.
